<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par117 />(an elliptical expression); thus e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּרַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=16}}, &c. (see the Lexicon) stands for {{GHGheb|text=כָּרַת בְּרִית}} like the English ''to close'' (sc. a bargain) with any one; {{GHGheb|text=נָטַר|translate=to keep}} (sc. {{GHGheb|text=אַף|translate=anger}}) equivalent to ''to be resentful'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=9}}, &c.; so also {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=5}} (beside {{GHGheb|text=נָטַר}}); {{GHGheb|text=נָשָׂא}} for {{GHGheb|text=נָשָׂא קוֹל|translate=to lift up the voice}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָשָׂא לְ}} for {{GHGheb|text=נָשָׂא עָוֹן לְ}} ''to take away any one’s sin'' (to forgive), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=24}}, 26, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלַח|translate=to put forth}} (sc. {{GHGheb|text=יָד|translate=the hand}}) equivalent to ''to reach after something'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=17}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|h}}
6. {{GHGterm|Verba sentiendi}} may take a second object, generally in the form of a participle or adjective and necessarily indeterminate, to define more exactly the action or state in which the object is perceived, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשְׁמַע משֶׁה אֶת־הָעָם בֹּכֶה|translate=and Moses heard the people weeping}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=אֽתְךָ רָאִ֫יתִי צַדִּיק|translate=thee have I seen righteous}}. Frequently, however, the second object is expressed by a separate clause. This is especially frequent with {{GHGheb|text=רָאָה|translate=to see}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=4}} ''and God saw the light, that it was good''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=25|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=8|verse=17|hidebook=1}}; so with {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע|translate=to know}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=8|hidebook=1}} (with two objects); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=5|verse=17}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|i}}
7. In certain instances {{GHGheb|text=את}} serves apparently to introduce or to emphasize a nominative. This cannot be regarded as a reappearance of the original substantival meaning of the {{GHGheb|text=את}}, since all unquestionable examples of the kind belong to the later Books of the Old Testament. They are rather (apart from textual errors or other explanations) cases of virtual dependence on an implied {{GHGterm|verbum regens}} understood. The constant use of {{GHGheb|text=את}} to indicate a clause governed by the verb, necessarily led at length to the use of {{GHGheb|text=את}} generally as a defining particle irrespective of a governing verb. So in the Hebrew of the Mishna<ref>Cf. Weiss, {{GHGheb|text=משפט לשון המשנה}} (Vienna, 1867), p. 112.</ref> (see above, {{GHGpar|3|a}}) {{GHGheb|text=אֹתוֹ}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֹתָהּ}} are prefixed even to a nominative without any special emphasis.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|k}}
Naturally the above does not apply to any of the places in which {{GHGheb|text=את}} is not the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}}, but a preposition (on {{GHGheb|text=את|translate=with}}, cf. {{GHGpar|103|b}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=34}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְאֶת־הַדּוֹב|translate=and that, with a bear}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}} here, however, has probably been interpolated from verse 36, where it is wanting); nor the places in which the accusative is subordinate to a passive (according to {{GHGpar|121|c}}) or to a verb of wanting as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=22|verse=17}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=32}}, see below, z. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=43|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=סָבִיב|translate=about}} governs like a verb, being followed by {{GHGheb|text=אוֹתָהּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|l}}
Other cases are clearly due to attraction to a following relative pronoun in the accusative ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=8|verse=17}}; but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=2|verse=5}}a, to {{GHGheb|text=ממצרים}}, must be omitted, with the LXX, as a later addition), or the accusative depends on a verbal idea, virtually contained in what has gone before, and consequently present to the speaker’s mind as governing the accusative. Thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=26}} (the verbal idea contained in {{GHGheb|text=ומשמרת}} verse 25 is ''they had to take charge of''); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=17|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=ויהי לְ}} implies ''it was given up'' or ''they gave him''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=16|translate=see where}} is equivalent to ''search now for''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=11|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=אל־ירע בעיניך}} is used in the sense of ''noli aegre ferre''<ref>So also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=13}} the Qal ({{GHGheb|text=יִיטַב}}) is, with Wellhausen, to be read instead of the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}.</ref>; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=36|verse=33|translate=and}} he had ''the brazier before him''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=3}} a verb like ''I esteem'' is mentally supplied before {{GHGheb|text=אֵת אֲשֶׁר}}. On {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=22|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=32}}, see below, aa.—Aposiopesis occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=11|verse=2|translate=for not your children}} (do I mean); still more boldly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=7}}, where either {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמַעְתֶּם}} or {{GHGheb|text=(תַּֽעֲשׂוּ) תִּשְׁמְעוּ}} is to be supplied.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|m}}
Setting aside a few undoubtedly corrupt passages<ref>Thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=16}}, where {{GHGheb|text=וְאֵי}} is to be read for {{GHGheb|text=וְאֶת}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=25}}, where at present the predicate of the relative clause is wanting; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=5}} the {{GHGheb|text=את}} is probably derived from a text which read the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=נָפַל}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=33}} instead of the artificial explanation ''what a burden'' (is, do ye ask?) we should read with the LXX and Vulg. {{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם הַמַּשָּׂא|translate=ye are the burden}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=מַרְאֵיהֶם וְאוֹתָם}} is unintelligible; in 37:19 read with Hitzig {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}} for {{GHGheb|text=את}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=2|verse=17}} for {{GHGheb|text=אתכם}} read with the LXX {{GHGheb|text=שֻֽׁבְכֶם}} [or {{GHGheb|text=אֵינְכֶם}}; for the {{GHGheb|text=אֶל}} cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=15|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=9}}].</ref> there still remain the<section end=par117 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
